title: Lizard: the child ties the bundles on the first three steps
wrong: The + bundle button builds a ten for the child, so tying ten sticks is only done on the first go.
done: On steps 1 to 3 there is no + bundle button; the child adds sticks and ties ten into a bundle each time.
why: Ten ones making one ten is the whole place-value idea, and it is skipped now.

title: Lizard: keep the child's attempt and draw the real bundles
wrong: A wrong try wipes the mat, never says what the child made, and shows a thinking emoji; the third wrong in a redo says nothing.
done: A wrong try keeps the child's bundles and sticks, says 'You made 34. We need 43.', draws their own mat, and caps at two tries then a look and redo.
why: The child sees their own model against the target, so the mistake teaches and rapid guessing stops working.

title: Pigeon: show the reason on the number line itself
wrong: The reason is a sentence and an emoji, the gap is never drawn, the line jumps when the panel opens, and the read arrow is a dot.
done: After the second wrong the line shows counted jumps from the child's mark to the right place, a real arrow on read goes, and the line stays still.
why: The gap between the child's answer and the right one is the whole lesson of a number line, and it must be seen on the line.

title: Pigeon: less help at the top, and four cards on closer goes
wrong: Top help writes every ten on the line so placing is copying, and closer goes have two cards so a guess is right half the time.
done: Top help writes only 0, the middle and the end, and closer goes have four cards with at most two sharing a tell.
why: Reading size from the picture and passing a step by knowing, not luck, is what the steps are meant to show.

title: Parrot: the see-saw tips toward the heavier side, and the words stop saying equals
wrong: True-or-false stays flat after a wrong answer, the post says = even when tipped, and a wrong stone count gets a vague line.
done: A wrong answer tips the see-saw toward the heavier side, = shows only when level, true-or-false asks 'Is it the same?', and stone slips are named.
why: The symbol must match the model: equal means level, and a wrong answer shows the weight difference.

title: Parrot: wrong cards from near misses, and a redo with no silly card
wrong: The right card is the only one not printed in the sum and never the biggest, and the redo adds the huge sum card.
done: Cards are the answer and close numbers, the answer sits in every position, and the redo offers the answer and the nearest card.
why: Card goes then need the balance idea, not a pattern, which is the main loophole in this game.
